Quick & Practical Hongbao Ideas** **A. Cash + Fun Extras (Best for Kids)** - **Cash Amount**: Use a round number (e.g., ¥20, ¥50, ¥100) based on your budget and the cousin’s age. Digital Hongbao (If You’re Short on Time)** - Send a **WeChat/Alipay red envelope** with a small amount (¥10–¥30) and pair it with a voice note saying: > *"春节快乐！祝你新年开心，长大后一定很厉害！"* (Happy Spring Festival! Wish you a happy new year and that you’ll grow up to be amazing!) - Add a **funny GIF** (e.g., a dancing panda or a "lucky cat" animation) to make it feel personal. **C. DIY Hongbao (For a Personal Touch)** - Use **red envelopes** (buy a pack from a stationery store or print one at home). Write a sweet note inside: > *"小朋友，祝你新年快乐，长大后当个大科学家/艺术家/运动员！"* (Little cousin, wish you a happy new year and that you’ll grow up to be a scientist/artist/athlete!) - Add a **hand-drawn picture** (even a simple one) or a **photo of you two** from a past holiday. --- ### **2. Delivery Tips** - **Last-Minute? No Problem!** - If you’re running late, **text them first** to let them know you’re sending something (even if it’s digital). Example: > *"叔叔/阿姨给你准备了红包，马上就到！"* (Uncle/Auntie is sending you a red envelope—it’s coming!) - For in-person delivery, **wrap it nicely** with red ribbon or a *福* (fú) character (symbolizing luck) on the envelope. - **If You Can’t Go In Person**: - Ask a family member to hand it over with a message like: > *"让他/她帮我转达祝福，说‘春节快乐，下次见面一起吃饺子！’"* (Have them pass along my wishes and say, "Happy Spring Festival! If You’re Really Short on Time…** - **Buy a pre-made hongbao**: Many convenience stores (e.g., *7-Eleven*, *FamilyMart*) sell small red envelopes with cash inside. Add a handwritten note or a sticker to personalize it. - **Use a "Group Hongbao"**: If you’re part of a family WeChat group, contribute to a **group red envelope** (e.g., ¥50–¥100 total) and explain it’s for the cousins.
